subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nanoparticle Inhalation Risks
description: A 60-second lesson on Nanoparticle Inhalation Risks.

hook.text: Breathe in nanoparticles and they travel from your lungs to your brain via the olfactory nerve — in hours.

buildup.text: Ultrafine particles deposit efficiently in the alveolar region — the deep lung where gas exchange occurs.

discovery.text: Inhaled nanoparticles trigger lung inflammation and can translocate to the bloodstream within minutes.

twist.text: Combustion nanoparticles from traffic are far more abundant than engineered ones — urban air is already full of them.

climax.text: PM0.1 monitoring is now recognized as critical — nano-fraction air pollution drives cardiovascular disease risk.

punchline.text: The smallest particles in the air cause the biggest health damage.

quiz.question: How can inhaled nanoparticles reach the brain?
options: They dissolve in saliva and are swallowed into the gut-brain axis
They travel via the olfactory nerve directly from the nasal passages to the brain
They are carried by white blood cells through the blood-brain barrier
